kept.body:
## [ISSUE] `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` called with no argument; the only overload takes a `UserModel`

**Severity:** HIGH — compilation failure in `services`, so nothing in this PR can build or run.

### The Problem
```java
// UsernameForm.java:47
if (context.getUser() != null && !isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()) {
```
The only declaration is in the superclass:
```java
// UsernamePasswordForm.java:160
protected boolean isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user) {
```
`grep -rn isConditionalPasskeysEnabled services/` finds no zero-arg overload anywhere in the hierarchy (`AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator`, `AbstractFormAuthenticator`). The HEAD commit, "Add user parameter requirement to isConditionalPasskeysEnabled method", added the parameter but did not update this call site.

### Theory / Proof
JLS 15.12.2: overload resolution needs an applicable method with a matching arity. No zero-arg method exists, so javac reports `method isConditionalPasskeysEnabled in class UsernamePasswordForm cannot be applied to given types; required: UserModel; found: no arguments`.

### What happens today vs. what will break
The `services` module fails to compile. All the new integration tests (`PasskeysUsernameFormTest.webauthnLoginWithDiscoverableKey_reauthentication` and the others) can't run.

### Research
The other two call sites in the same PR (`UsernamePasswordForm.java:115`, `:137`) pass `context.getUser()`. This one should do the same.

### Recommendation
```java
if (context.getUser() != null && !isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())) {
```
(See the companion comment on `UsernamePasswordForm.java:161`: the predicate itself also needs fixing.)

There is no zero-arg overload, varargs version or default method. HEAD commit 3214b188 changed the signature without updating this caller, so compilation fails.

kept.claim: isConditionalPasskeysEnabled requires user != null, so on a normal first login (no user in context) webauthnAuth.fillContextForm is never called, which removes conditional-UI passkey login from the username/password and username forms.
kept.body:
## [ISSUE] `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled` requires `user != null`, which turns passkeys off for normal (non-re-auth) login

**Severity:** HIGH — regression: passkey login no longer works on the ordinary login page, which is the main passkeys use case.

### The Problem
```java
// UsernamePasswordForm.java:160-162
protected boolean isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user) {
    return webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled() && user != null;
}
```
Both callers pass `context.getUser()`:
- `authenticate()` line 115: `if (isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())) webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context);`
- `challenge(ctx, error, field)` line 137: same guard.

In a normal browser flow, nobody has identified the user yet when `UsernamePasswordForm.authenticate` runs, so `context.getUser() == null` (this is the `else` branch at line 103). The predicate returns `false`, and `fillContextForm` never runs. `ENABLE_WEBAUTHN_CONDITIONAL_UI`, `CHALLENGE`, `RP_ID`, etc. are never set on the form, and the `//form[@id='webauth']` conditional-UI form is not rendered.

### Theory / Proof
- Before this PR, `authenticate()` filled the webauthn context in the **`user == null`** branch ("setup webauthn data when the user is not already selected"), and `challenge()` guarded on `context.getUser() == null`. The PR's goal is to *also* enable passkeys when a user is already set (re-auth). The new condition instead *replaces* the null case with the non-null case.
- `WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator.shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators` now returns `false`, so `fillContextForm` works for both a null and a non-null user. No null guard is needed.
- `action()` (line 59) still accepts webauthn submissions based only on `isPasskeysEnabled()`. So the server would validate a passkey assertion, but the page never gets a challenge for the browser to sign.

### What happens today vs. what will break
With passkeys enabled, `oauth.openLoginForm()` on a fresh session shows a plain username/password page with no passkey autofill. Existing tests that rely on it will fail, e.g. `PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest.webauthnLoginWithDiscoverableKey` (line 83), which expects the discoverable key to log the user in automatically. The new `*_reauthentication` tests also do an initial passkey login before the `prompt=login` step, so they fail at that first step. The same applies to `UsernameForm` (same superclass `authenticate`).

### Research
The re-auth scenario (OIDC `prompt=login`, `max_age`) needs passkeys *in addition to* first-factor login. The WebAuthn Level 3 conditional mediation model (`mediation: "conditional"`) is meant for the initial identifier-entry page, so dropping it there defeats the feature.

### Recommendation
Drop the user check. `fillContextForm` already handles both cases via `shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators`:
```java
protected boolean isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel currentUser) {
    return webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled();
}
```
If the parameter is kept for subclasses, document that `null` means "user not yet identified" and must return `true` when passkeys are enabled.
